note: Unselected T2D; four Phase 2 programmes (LY2409021/adomeglivant, MK-3577, PF-06291874, volagidemab) all lowered glucose as the animals predicted and all stopped on the same unpredicted transaminase, LDL-C, blood-pressure and liver-fat cluster; no member reached Phase 3 or a filing, so there is no FDA review for any of them.
label: Type 2 diabetes (GCGR antagonist)

engagement.model: Anti-GCGR antibody in ob/ob and C57BL/6 mice and cynomolgus monkeys
engagement.note: Amgen anti-GCGR mAb B normalised ob/ob glucose for 8 days after one 3 mg/kg dose and raised glucagon and active GLP-1 in monkeys; no human comparison yet.
engagement.short: mAb normalised ob/ob glucose for 8 days
engagement.quote: In normal cynomolgus monkeys, a single injection improved glucose tolerance while increasing glucagon and active glucagon-like peptide-1 levels.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. REMD-477/volagidemab is Amgen's AMG 477 (licensed to REMD in 2013), but the paper does not say its mAb B is AMG 477, so product_in_model is false.

engagement.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
engagement.note: Merck's GRA1 (sibling of MK-3577) blocked exogenous-glucagon hyperglycaemia in humanised-GCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; Pfizer's PF-06291874 did the same in rats in 2013. No human comparison yet.
engagement.quote: When administered orally to hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys, GRA1 blocked hyperglycemic responses to exogenous glucagon.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. No preclinical paper on LY2409021 or MK-3577 itself was found; the published small-molecule model package is GRA1 (Merck) and PF-06291874 (Pfizer, doi:10.1016/j.bmcl.2013.03.014).

engagement.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
engagement.note: MK-3577 blunted the glucagon-challenge glucose rise in 36 healthy subjects (Imax 0.96, IC50 13.9 nM), as the rodent and monkey challenge predicted; LY2409021 showed the same in 2015.
engagement.quote: The drug effect was modeled by using an inhibitory E max model (I max = 0.96 and IC50 = 13.9 nM) to reduce the ability of glucagon to increase the glucose production rate (GPROD).
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing of a healthy-volunteer glucagon challenge with the Mu 2012 sibling-compound model. The Merck Phase 1 challenge study has no ClinicalTrials.gov record under MK-3577, so registry_date is null.
engagement.judgement: Called same: the model readout (block of an exogenous-glucagon glucose excursion) was run in people and moved as predicted. readout_tier is direct because an in-vivo glucagon challenge is a blockade of a stimulus at the target; a stricter reader would call the glucose readout downstream. The humans were dosed with MK-3577 and the animals with GRA1/PF-06291874, so product_in_model is false. Kelly 2015 (doi:10.1111/dom.12446) reproduces this with LY2409021 and is not entered separately.
engagement.magnitude_basis: fraction of the glucagon-evoked glucose rise blocked

engagement.model: Anti-GCGR antibody in ob/ob and C57BL/6 mice and cynomolgus monkeys
engagement.note: Amgen's Phase 1 of AMG 477 (now volagidemab) in healthy volunteers: one injection cut fasting glucose 10-15% for up to four weeks, the direction the mouse and monkey antibody data predicted.
engagement.quote: In the phase 1 clinical study conducted by Amgen in healthy volunteers, a single injection of REMD-477 (then known as AMG477) reduced fasting glucose levels by 10 to 15 percent for up to four weeks.
engagement.confidence_note: Trade-press reproduction of the sponsor's statement; the Amgen Phase 1 is unpublished and has no registry record found; dated to the news item (2015), the result may have been public earlier. Pettus 2018 (T1D, doi:10.1111/dom.13202) later reproduced the glucose and glucagon response in patients.
engagement.reason: Fasting glucose fell as mice predicted
engagement.judgement: Healthy volunteers count for engagement. Tier 5 patient side (sponsor statement carried by trade press) paired by the drafter with Yan 2009 as model side; scored low confidence, trial_unreported. The T2D dose-escalation NCT02455011 (75 patients, completed) never posted results, so no patient-level T2D engagement datum exists.
engagement.magnitude_basis: fasting glucose fall (mice normalised vs 10-15% in volunteers)

engagement.model: Glucagon challenge in healthy overweight cats (MK-3577)
engagement.note: Ten years after the human challenge data, 3 mg/kg MK-3577 blunted the glucagon-stimulated glucose and insulin rise in five cats: reproduces the 2014 human result, predicts nothing new.
engagement.short: Cat glucagon challenge retrodicts human blockade
engagement.quote: At a dose of 3 mg/kg, MK-3577 blunted the glucagon-stimulated rise of glucose (p=0.0089) and insulin (p=0.02).
engagement.confidence_note: Veterinary pharmacology study (n=5 healthy cats) run for feline diabetes, not for the human programme; abstract-level. Entered because it is a model dosed with a member drug after the human answer was known (decision 10).
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: the cat challenge was run in 2024 with the 2014 human glucagon-challenge result already published, so retro, not same. Drafter's pairing (comparison_stated false). It is the only animal study with MK-3577 itself in the public record.

dose.model: Anti-GCGR antibody in ob/ob and C57BL/6 mice and cynomolgus monkeys
dose.note: Mouse effective dose was a single 3 mg/kg injection; the only T2D dose-escalation of REMD-477 (NCT02455011, 75 patients, completed 2016) never reported exposure or results.
dose.short: Mouse 3 mg/kg; human T2D dose unreported
dose.quote: A single injection of a lead antibody, mAb B, at 3 mg/kg, normalized blood glucose levels in ob/ob mice for 8 days.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. T1D dosing (70 mg single dose, 35-70 mg weekly) is published but dose is tied to efficacy, which has no T2D trial to score against.
dose.judgement: Left untested rather than imported from T1D: dose is scored against the efficacy of the context's disease, and no T2D efficacy result for volagidemab is public. No tolerability margin was stated in the mouse work (margin_stated false).

dose.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
dose.note: PF-06291874's exposure target was set at concentrations matching its rat in-vitro potency, with 'excellent overall in vivo safety' claimed but no numerical margin; no patient exposure yet.
dose.quote: In a rat glucagon challenge model, it was shown to reduce the glucagon-elicited glucose excursion in a dose-dependent manner and at a concentration consistent with its rat in vitro potency.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the rat effective concentration is not given in the abstract.

dose.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
dose.note: Once-daily 5-150 mg PF-06291874 gave dose-proportional exposure (t1/2 ~20 h) and dose-dependent glucose lowering in T2D; 30-100 mg then cut HbA1c, so the pharmacological target was reached and worked.
dose.short: Target reached; glucose and HbA1c fell
dose.quote: Day 14 fasting plasma glucose and mean daily glucose values were reduced from baseline in a dose-dependent manner, with placebo-corrected decreases of 34.3 and 42.4 mg/dl, respectively, at the 150 mg dose.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; neither abstract tabulates the rat effective concentration against human exposure, so 'reached' is inferred from dose-dependent PD and the later HbA1c result, not from a numerical match.
dose.judgement: Scored same under the 'reached, drug worked' row: human exposure produced the modelled pharmacology and the 12-week HbA1c primary endpoint was met (Kazierad 2018, NCT02554877). The transaminase, LDL-C and blood-pressure rises occurred at the effective dose but did not stop dosing to target, so they are counted once, in safety, and dose carries no blocked_by. margin_stated false because 'excellent overall in vivo safety' names no NOAEL or tolerated multiple. registry_date is the MAD study NCT01856595 (results posted 2018-11-01).

efficacy.model: Anti-GCGR antibody in ob/ob and C57BL/6 mice and cynomolgus monkeys
efficacy.note: Five weeks of anti-GCGR mAb normalised non-fasting glucose in DIO mice; the only T2D trial of volagidemab (NCT02455011) never reported, so the antibody arm stays uncompared in T2D.
efficacy.short: mAb normalised DIO-mouse glucose at 5 weeks
efficacy.quote: In the present study, we demonstrate that a 5-week treatment of diet-induced obese mice with mAb effectively normalized nonfasting blood glucose.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. T1D results (HbA1c -0.5%, Pettus 2022) are another disease and do not score here.
efficacy.judgement: Untested, not an empty cell: a model existed and was used, and the T2D comparison (NCT02455011, Phase 1/2 dose-escalation, 75 patients, completed) was never published or posted.

efficacy.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
efficacy.note: Acute and chronic GRA1 (sibling of MK-3577) lowered glucose in several diabetic mouse models, with modest glucagon and GLP-1 rises; no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: GRA1 lowered glucose in diabetic mice
efficacy.quote: In several murine models of diabetes, acute and chronic dosing with GRA1 significantly reduced blood glucose concentrations and moderately increased plasma glucagon and glucagon-like peptide-1.

efficacy.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
efficacy.note: LY2409021 cut HbA1c 0.65-0.83% at 12 weeks and up to 0.92% at 24 weeks (primary endpoints met); MK-3577 and PF-06291874 then replicated, so the diabetic-mouse glucose prediction held for every member tested.
efficacy.quote: After 12 weeks, least squares (LS) mean change from baseline in HbA1c was -0.83% (10 mg), -0.65% (30 mg), and -0.66% (60 mg) (all P < 0.05) vs. placebo, 0.11%.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing. No preclinical paper on LY2409021 itself was found, so the model side is the sibling GRA1/PF-06291874 package. Online 2015-12-19, print 2016.
efficacy.reason: HbA1c fell as diabetic mice predicted
efficacy.judgement: Same, not neg: no GCGR antagonist that lowered glucose in diabetic mice failed on glucose in patients; the class died on safety, so efficacy keeps its match. Magnitude direction_only because mice normalised glucose while patients got 0.8-0.9% HbA1c. Registry results for the two Kazda trials were posted only in 2018-04-24; the MK-3577 crossover (NCT00868790, results 2017-01-11, weighted mean glucose -18.8/-25.0 vs -1.6 mg/dL placebo) and PF-06291874 (NCT02554877, results 2017-08-07) are carried in patient_trials and change no status. No outcome trial was ever run (outcome_tested null).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: glucose normalisation in diabetic mice vs 0.8-0.9% HbA1c fall in patients

patient_trials.quote: After 12 weeks, least squares (LS) mean change from baseline in HbA1c was -0.83% (10 mg), -0.65% (30 mg), and -0.66% (60 mg) (all P < 0.05) vs. placebo, 0.11%.
After 24 weeks, LS mean change from baseline in HbA1c was -0.45% (2.5 mg), -0.78% (10 mg, P < 0.05), -0.92% (20 mg, P < 0.05), and -0.15% with placebo.

Registry primary outcome, change from baseline after 4-week treatment in weighted mean glucose (mg/dL): placebo -1.6, MK-3577 QD AM -18.8, MK-3577 QD PM -25.0, metformin -36.5 (transcribed from the results table).
Dose-dependent mean reductions from baseline in HbA1c for PF-06291874 ranged from -0.67% (-7.29 mmol/mol) to -0.93% (-10.13 mmol/mol), and for FPG from -16.6 to -33.3 mg/dL after 12 weeks of dosing.

efficacy.note: Whole-body Gcgr deletion lowered fed and fasted glucose and improved oral glucose tolerance; the genetic ceiling for antagonist efficacy, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: Blood glucose levels were somewhat reduced in GR(-/-) mice relative to wild type, in both the fed and fasted state.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. First Gcgr-/- report (BBRC, January 2002); Gelling 2003 (doi:10.1073/pnas.0237106100) is the fuller characterisation. No FDA review exists for any member, so model_filed is null.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the knockout's first use. The system is the genetic counterpart of full receptor antagonism, not a dosed model, so no member compound can be in it (product_in_model false) and no dose entry is possible.

efficacy.note: LY2409021 cut HbA1c 0.65-0.83% at 12 weeks, the direction the knockout's lower glucose and STZ-resistance predicted; MK-3577 and PF-06291874 replicated.
efficacy.short: HbA1c fell as the knockout predicted
efficacy.quote: After 12 weeks, least squares (LS) mean change from baseline in HbA1c was -0.83% (10 mg), -0.65% (30 mg), and -0.66% (60 mg) (all P < 0.05) vs. placebo, 0.11%.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing of the knockout (Conarello 2007 as the diabetic-setting model side: 'Gcgr (-/-) mice were resistant to STZ-induced hyperglycaemia') with the first member Phase 2. Online 2015-12-17, print 2016; registry results for NCT00871572 and NCT01241448 both posted 2018-04-24.
efficacy.judgement: Same, direction only: a lifelong knockout cannot give an effect size for a 12-week drug trial. Dated to the first member efficacy result (Kazda 2016), not to the earlier non-member MK-0893 Phase 2.

patient_trials.quote: LY2409021 produced reductions in HbA1c that were significantly different from placebo over both 12 and 24 weeks.

efficacy.model: Semi-mechanistic glucose-to-HbA1c models (ADOPT, FFH, FHH, IGRH) fitted to LY2409021 Phase 1b
efficacy.note: Four semi-mechanistic HbA1c models built on 4-week LY2409021 PK, glucose and HbA1c data to project 24-week HbA1c before the comparison is made.
efficacy.quote: The models were built using LY2409021 pharmacokinetics, glucose, and HbA1c data from a 4-week Phase 1b study.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use; the comparison is in the same paper. Built in 2025 on a programme that stopped in 2017, so it is a retrodiction by construction.

efficacy.model: Semi-mechanistic glucose-to-HbA1c models (ADOPT, FFH, FHH, IGRH) fitted to LY2409021 Phase 1b
efficacy.note: FHH and IGRH models reproduced the 24-week Phase 2b HbA1c fall within 0.1%; ADOPT and FFH over-predicted by 0.29% and 0.15%.
efficacy.quote: Overall, the FHH and IGRH models closely predicted the mean ΔHbA1c at Week 24 within 0.1% difference from the observed values in the Phase 2b study.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open access, abstract-level. The 24-week Phase 2b is NCT01241448 (LY2409021 2.5-20 mg, Kazda 2016), results posted 2018-04-24. Two of the four candidate models over-predicted; the source calls the transit-compartment models the match.
efficacy.judgement: Retro, not same: the 24-week result was published in 2015 and the models were evaluated against it in 2025. Within 2x on the stated quantity (mean change in HbA1c at week 24). Class-level: it predicts the regimen's HbA1c, not which patients respond. A dose entry is not opened because the paper chose no human dose.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: mean change in HbA1c at week 24, model-estimated vs observed

safety.model: Anti-GCGR antibody in ob/ob and C57BL/6 mice and cynomolgus monkeys
safety.note: Eighteen weeks of anti-GCGR mAb in mice predicted reversible hyperglucagonaemia and mild alpha-cell hyperplasia with no neoplasia; silent on liver enzymes, lipids and blood pressure.
safety.quote: Long-term treatment with the mAb caused dose-dependent hyperglucagonemia and minimal to mild alpha-cell hyperplasia in lean mice.

safety.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
safety.note: Pfizer's rat/dog package called PF-06291874 safe; the Merck sibling package predicted only hyperglucagonaemia and a GLP-1 rise; nothing on transaminases, LDL-C, blood pressure or liver fat.
safety.quote: resulting in excellent selectivity in broad-panel screening, lower cytotoxicity, and excellent overall in vivo safety in early pre-clinical testing.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the clause is quoted verbatim from a longer sentence. The toxicology species and findings are not given.

safety.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
safety.note: 28-day LY2409021 raised aminotransferases dose-dependently in T2D patients, a harm rats and dogs can show and the preclinical packages did not flag; hyperglucagonaemia was the one predicted effect that appeared.
safety.short: ALT rise missed by rat/dog package
safety.quote: Serum aminotransferases increased in a dose-dependent manner with multiple dosing and reversed after cessation of dosing.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; the model side is PF-06291874's package because no LY2409021 animal data are published. The 28-day study appears to be NCT01606397, which posted no results, so registry_date is null.
safety.judgement: Contra by silence contradicted: rats and dogs show transaminase rises readily, and the published package claimed excellent in-vivo safety. The matched prediction (hyperglucagonaemia, Mu 2012; 'glucagon levels increased', Kelly 2015) does not rescue the track because one contra beats one same. Alpha-cell hyperplasia, the other mouse prediction, has never been assessable in patients and is neither credited nor charged.

safety.model: Glucagon-challenge hGCGR mice and rhesus monkeys; diabetic mice (small-molecule GRAs)
safety.note: PF-06291874 itself, the compound the rat package called safe, raised LDL-C and aminotransferases; blood pressure, weight and liver-fat rises (Kazda 2017, Guzman 2017) followed, all unpredicted; every programme stopped.
safety.short: LDL-C and ALT rises with the modelled compound
safety.quote: Small dose-dependent increases in LDL cholesterol were observed, along with reversible increases in serum aminotransferases that were largely within the laboratory reference range.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled. Registry AE tables for LY2409021 (NCT01241448: ALT increased 4/65, 7/66, 4/66 vs 1/66 placebo) and PF-06291874 (NCT02554877) corroborate. Later harms: ambulatory SBP +2.3 mm Hg (Kazda 2017, doi:10.1111/dom.12904), hepatic fat fraction +4.4% and ALT +10.7 U/L (Guzman 2017, doi:10.1111/dom.12958), small LDL-C and BP rises with PF-06291874 at 12 weeks (Kazierad 2018, doi:10.1111/dom.13440).
safety.judgement: Strengthens the 2015 contra with the modelled compound itself (product_in_model true). The LDL-C rise was later reproduced in mice with Merck's MK-0893 plus structurally diverse GRAs and traced to cholesterol absorption (Guan 2015, doi:10.1194/jlr.M060897), proving the species could have shown it; that paper is a retrodiction of a non-member's trial result and is not scored as an entry under the member-only rule. Gcgr-/- mice develop fasting hepatic steatosis, but no member's package reported it before the human liver-fat finding, so it is not credited either.

safety.model: Anti-GCGR antibody in ob/ob and C57BL/6 mice and cynomolgus monkeys
safety.note: One 70 mg dose of REMD-477 in 21 T1D patients nearly tripled fasting glucagon, reversibly, as the mouse mAb predicted; no lipid, BP or weight change after a single dose. Imported from T1D.
safety.quote: Fasting plasma glucagon increased from 20.2 to 56.3 pmol/L, 2 weeks after REMD-477 treatment (p=0.01) and returned to baseline by 8 weeks.
safety.confidence_note: Imported from T1D (NCT02715193, no registry results posted); quote from the PMC author manuscript (PMC6181222). Online 2017-12-29, print 2018. Single dose only, so the 12-week harms could not yet show.
safety.judgement: Safety comparisons transfer across indications (imported_from MONDO:0005147). Scored same because the mouse prediction (reversible hyperglucagonaemia) held in direction and reversibility; alpha-cell hyperplasia was not assessable.
safety.magnitude_basis: fasting glucagon rise (mouse dose-dependent vs 2.8-fold in patients)

safety.model: Anti-GCGR antibody in ob/ob and C57BL/6 mice and cynomolgus monkeys
safety.note: Twelve weeks of weekly volagidemab in 79 T1D patients raised transaminases, LDL-C and blood pressure, harms the 18-week mouse mAb study could have shown and did not; the same cluster as the small molecules. Imported from T1D.
safety.quote: No increase in hypoglycemia was observed with volagidemab therapy; however, increases in serum transaminases, low-density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol and blood pressure were observed.
safety.confidence_note: Imported from T1D (NCT03117998, results posted 2023-05-25); abstract-level. The T2D dose-escalation NCT02455011 posted no safety data.
safety.judgement: Contra by silence contradicted, on the same harms that sank the small molecules: mice can show transaminase rises, LDL-C rises (shown with small-molecule GRAs by Guan 2015) and blood pressure, and the 18-week mAb study reported none. Dated to the Nature Medicine online publication (2022-10-03), earlier than the registry posting. The track turns from same to contra; it cannot turn back without a tier 1-4 source showing the harm attenuated to background.

safety.note: Knockout predicted ~100-fold hyperglucagonaemia with near-normal glycaemia and normal lipids; alpha-cell hyperplasia (Gelling 2003), PNETs (Yu 2011) and 'adverse lipid changes' (Yang 2011) followed.
safety.quote: Plasma glucagon levels were strikingly elevated in both fed and fasted animals.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The track's later predictions, all before any member patient result: alpha-cell hyperplasia (Gelling 2003, doi:10.1073/pnas.0237106100), lean and steatosis-resistant on high-fat diet (Conarello 2007, doi:10.1007/s00125-006-0481-3), raised hepatic triglyceride secretion on fasting (Longuet 2008, doi:10.1016/j.cmet.2008.09.008), PNETs by 10-12 months (Yu 2011, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0023397), raised plasma amino acids, cholesterol and bile acids with 'adverse lipid changes' (Yang 2011, doi:10.1186/1471-2164-12-281).
safety.judgement: Opening entry. Modality left null: every harm the knockout can speak to is on-target, which the brief pools across modalities.

safety.note: 28-day LY2409021 raised glucagon and lowered glucose with minimal hypoglycaemia in T2D, as the knockout's hyperglucagonaemia-without-hypoglycaemia predicted; alpha-cell hyperplasia not assessable.
safety.quote: Fasting and postprandial glucose were reduced and glucagon levels increased after single and multiple dosing, with reductions in fasting serum glucose of up to ∼1.25 mmol/l on day 28.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Gelling 2003. Kelly 2015 gives no glucagon fold-change, so magnitude is direction only (the knockout's two-orders-of-magnitude rise is far larger than any dosed-human value). The 28-day study NCT01606397 posted no results.
safety.judgement: Same on the knockout's first stated harm (hyperglucagonaemia) and on its glycaemic safety (near-normal glycaemia, 'minimal hypoglycaemia'). The transaminase rise is not charged here: the knockout papers reported no liver enzymes in their abstracts, and a knockout characterisation is not a toxicology screen; its stated predictions govern.

safety.note: PF-06291874 raised LDL-C and gluconeogenic amino acids in T2D, the 'adverse lipid changes' and hyperaminoacidaemia Yang 2011 read off the knockout liver five years earlier.
safety.short: Knockout's lipid and amino-acid warning held
safety.quote: Small dose-dependent increases in LDL cholesterol were observed, along with reversible increases in serum aminotransferases that were largely within the laboratory reference range.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Yang 2011 ('increased amino acids, cholesterol, and bile acid levels ... may be associated with adverse lipid changes', online 2011-06-01). Online 2016-05-12; NCT01856595 results posted 2018-11-01. Kazierad 2016 also reports 'An increase in circulating gluconeogenic amino acids was also observed on days 2 and 14.'
safety.judgement: Strengthens the match with a prospective prediction the dosed-animal packages did not make: the knockout polyomics named cholesterol and amino acids as the liabilities of full antagonism before any member reported them. Kazda 2017 and Guzman 2017 later reproduced the lipid rise with LY2409021.
safety.magnitude_basis: direction of plasma cholesterol and amino-acid change

safety.note: Six months of LY2409021 raised liver fat 4.4%, ALT, weight and blood pressure in T2D; the high-fat-fed knockout was lean and steatosis-resistant, the opposite prediction.
safety.short: Patients gained fat and weight; knockout lean
safety.quote: LY2409021 was also associated with significant increases in systolic blood pressure vs sitagliptin (4.9 mm Hg; P = .030) and vs placebo (4.3 mm Hg; P = .029), as well as significant increases in body weight and total cholesterol.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Conarello 2007 ('decreased body weight and food intake ... resistant to the development of hepatic steatosis' on high-fat diet). Online 2017-06-08; NCT02111096 (terminated, n=174) results posted 2018-04-24. Hepatic fat fraction +4.44% vs placebo and ALT +10.7 U/L are in the same abstract.
safety.reason: Weight and liver fat went the other way
safety.judgement: Contra, magnitude opposite: on body weight and liver fat the knockout predicted the wrong direction for the setting closest to T2D patients (high-fat-fed), and one wrong prediction beats the same-track matches on glucagon and cholesterol. Longuet 2008 (fasting raised hepatic triglyceride secretion) points the other way, so the liver-fat call rests on the fed phenotype; weight is unambiguous. Blood pressure, never a knockout readout, is neither credited nor charged; PNETs (Yu 2011) are untestable in six-month trials. The track cannot turn back without a tier 1-4 source showing the harms attenuated.
safety.magnitude_basis: direction of body weight and hepatic fat change

safety.model: Mahvash disease: homozygous GCGR loss-of-function in humans
safety.note: First human homozygous GCGR loss-of-function (P86S): marked hyperglucagonaemia, alpha-cell hyperplasia and an islet tumour without glucagonoma syndrome; the human-genetic read-out of lifelong antagonism.
safety.short: Human GCGR loss: hyperglucagonaemia, islet tumour
safety.quote: We hereby report the first homozygous missense mutation in the human GCGR, which is associated with alpha cell hyperplasia and hyperglucagonemia.
safety.confidence_note: Open access (PMC2767399), abstract-level reading. Print 2009-11, no earlier online date in Europe PMC. Yu 2011 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0023397) adds that the same patient 'further develops pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors'.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at the first case. A single patient with a lifelong loss of function; no drug is in the system, so product_in_model is false and dose does not apply.

safety.model: Mahvash disease: homozygous GCGR loss-of-function in humans
safety.note: GRA-dosed T2D patients showed the Mahvash hyperglucagonaemia within 28 days with minimal hypoglycaemia; alpha-cell hyperplasia and PNET risk cannot show in short trials.
safety.quote: Fasting and postprandial glucose were reduced and glucagon levels increased after single and multiple dosing, with reductions in fasting serum glucose of up to ∼1.25 mmol/l on day 28.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Zhou 2009. The 28-day study NCT01606397 posted no results. A second human loss-of-function case (Larger 2016, doi:10.1530/EDM-16-0081, online 2016-11-21) adds hyperaminoacidaemia and no hypoglycaemia, after Kazierad 2016 had already reported the amino-acid rise with PF-06291874, so it changes no status.
safety.judgement: Same, direction only, on the one Mahvash feature a drug trial can reach (hyperglucagonaemia). Not charged for silence on transaminases, lipids or blood pressure: a single case report is not a negative screen, and PNET, the harm this system uniquely predicts, is untestable in trials of six months. Prediction level stays class; Mahvash does not select responders.

safety.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)
safety.note: Mice dosed with MK-0893 and other GRAs raised LDL-C through GLP-2-linked cholesterol absorption, abolished by ezetimibe; predicts an on-target LDL-C rise for every antagonist.
safety.short: Mouse traces GRA LDL-C to absorption
safety.quote: To examine potential pharmacologic mitigation, coadministration of ezetimibe (a potent inhibitor of cholesterol absorption) in mice abrogated the GRA-associated increase of LDL-c.
safety.confidence_note: Open access (PMC4617405) but the full-text fetch returned nothing, so abstract-level: the 'structurally diverse GRAs' are not named and none is known to be a member (product_in_model false). Online 2015-09-15, print 2015-11.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. The model was built to explain MK-0893's human LDL-C rise, a non-member result, so that retrodiction is not scored; its member predictions from 2015-09-15 onward are prospective (decision 10). Modality null: the mechanism is on-target, so the harm pools across antibody and small molecule.

safety.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)
safety.note: PF-06291874, a member the model never saw, raised LDL-C dose-dependently in T2D within 14-28 days, as the cholesterol-absorption mouse predicted.
safety.short: LDL-C rise appeared with first member
safety.quote: Small dose-dependent increases in LDL cholesterol were observed, along with reversible increases in serum aminotransferases that were largely within the laboratory reference range.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing. Online 2016-05-12, eight months after the model; NCT01856595 results posted 2018-11-01. No member LDL-C datum was found public before 2015-09-15 (Kelly 2015 and Kazda 2016 abstracts report none), but a conference abstract could not be excluded.
safety.judgement: Prospective same for the class: the first member LDL-C report post-dates the model. Direction only; neither abstract gives a comparable LDL-C magnitude.

safety.note: Six weeks of LY2409021 20 mg raised serum lipids in 270 T2D patients at a dose that lowered HbA1c; second member, same on-target lipid rise.

safety.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)
safety.note: Twelve weeks of the antibody volagidemab raised LDL-C in T1D: the harm follows the target, not the chemotype, as cholesterol absorption implies. Imported from T1D.
safety.quote: No increase in hypoglycemia was observed with volagidemab therapy; however, increases in serum transaminases, low-density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol and blood pressure were observed.

safety.judgement: Strengthens with a third member and the other modality; safety comparisons transfer across indications (imported_from MONDO:0005147).
